entities.name: Raoul of Turenne
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Raoul (Rodulf) of Turenne, archbishop of Bourges from 840 until his death on June 21, 866, was a pivotal ecclesiastical figure in Carolingian Francia during the tumultuous mid-9th century. Operating within the fragmented successor states of Charlemagne's empire, he distinguished himself as a skilled diplomat, a rigorous proponent of monastic and clerical reform, and a significant patron of learning. His career unfolded amidst the reigns of Charles the Bald and Lothair I, where his influence extended beyond his archiepiscopal see, shaping both church policy and political alliances in West Francia.

Elevated to the archiepiscopal see of Bourges in 840, Raoul immediately engaged in extensive efforts to restore discipline and intellectual rigor to the clergy and monastic communities within his metropolitan province. He presided over several synods, including the Council of Tours in 844, where significant canons on ecclesiastical discipline were promulgated. As a trusted advisor to Charles the Bald, Raoul undertook numerous diplomatic missions, notably negotiating peace agreements and mediating disputes between the Carolingian brothers, such as during the partition of Verdun in 843 and the subsequent Treaty of Meerssen in 847. He was also instrumental in promoting the veneration of local saints and fostering scriptoria, enhancing the cultural and spiritual life of his diocese.
